newsitem.title: UK: Shipowners call for global bunker sulphur standard.
newsitem.headline: Shipowners call for global bunker sulphur standard.

text.p: Shipowners called on Tuesday for a global cap on sulphur pollution caused by fuel burned by their vessels rather than two-tier controls with stringent provisions aimed at protecting particular regions.

The International Chamber of Shipping (ICS) said it will call for a single standard at an international meeting to set sulphur content in bunker fuels and the emission of sulphur oxides (SOx) by ships.

ICS said it "urged that a single, practical worldwide standard for sulphur content of bunker fuels should be introduced, which will benefit the world as a whole, and avoid the problems which will otherwise apply if local or regional emission control areas are established."

An International Maritime Organization (IMO) conference on atmospheric pollution to be held in London in September is to consider setting a global cap on sulphur fuel emission of five percent with a lower level of 1.5 percent to protect special regions, such as the Baltic and North Sea.
ICS is proposing that a single limit of 3.5 percent should be set now, but be reduced to three percent over an agreed timescale.

Marine director of the ICS Captain John Joyce said the proposed five percent upper cap for the IMO regulations might be interpreted as an acceptance of a lowering of global standards when the present average of sulphur emissions from ships is about three percent.
"There could also be real problems with policing such complex arrangements, while unnecessary sulphur emission outside control areas will continue to cause environmental damage," he said.

Joyce said it would be difficult for ships to carry two different grades of fuel which might also be hard to obtain outside control areas. The cost of handling different bunker fuels would also fall exclusively on shipowners, he added. --Paul Berrill Reuters Shipping News + 44 171 542 4087. Fax 542 5017
